title: Machine-readable copy of product pages
question: Can an agent get a product page as Markdown instead of HTML?
method: GET the first sampled product page with an Accept header that prefers text/markdown and accepts text/html at q=0.9. Pass when the response is text/markdown and names the product (its Product name or title appears in the body). Warn when that response sends no Vary: Accept (or Vary: *), because a shared cache may then serve Markdown to browsers. Otherwise follow a Markdown alternate the HTML links (link rel=alternate type=text/markdown), then the page URL with .md appended, within three requests in all, and pass when either answers text/markdown that names the product. Fail when none does, and fail when a response labelled text/markdown is HTML (its body opens with a tag or carries a doctype or <html> near the top): converted Markdown starts with front matter or a heading, never with markup. Skipped when no product page was sampled. Coding agents request Markdown today, but search crawlers do not, hence the low weight.

spec.title: RFC 7763 text/markdown media type

title: Server-rendered product content
question: Are title, price and description present in the raw HTML without JavaScript?
method: Parse the raw HTML of the sampled product pages that answered, without running JavaScript. A page is complete when it carries a title (a <title> or a Product name in JSON-LD), a price (a JSON-LD offer price, an amount with a currency in the text, or an element with a price class) and a description (a meta description, a JSON-LD description or more than 80 words of text). Pass when every page is complete, warn when only some are, fail when none is (an empty app shell). Fail as well when a product URL lands on a sign-in or password page (it was redirected to a login or password path, or what answered is a password form with no product content): Google's landing-page rules say a product page must not require registration or sign-in, and Shopify's password page makes a store ineligible for agentic storefronts. A product page that merely links to the account area is a product page. A page that could not be fetched is named and never scored. Skipped when no product page was sampled or none could be fetched.

spec.title: Google: JavaScript SEO basics
Google Merchant Center: the link attribute and its landing page requirements

title: Page weight within crawler limits
question: Does a product page fit in what crawlers read, and answer quickly enough to be crawled at scale?
method: Measure the uncompressed HTML of each sampled product page that answered (the home page when none were sampled) and its response time. Googlebot reads the first 2 MB of a document, headers included, and ignores every byte after it. The scanner stops reading at the same size. Fail when a page reaches 2 MB (2,000,000 bytes) or was cut off: whatever follows the cutoff, including structured data placed at the end of the body, is not indexed. Warn when a page is 1 MB or more, or when the slowest response took 3 s or more. Pass below 1 MB and 3 s. Response time is a crawl-health hint, not an eligibility rule. Skipped when product pages were sampled but none could be fetched.

spec.title: Google: Googlebot (file size limits)
Google Search Central blog: crawler file size limits explained (2026)

title: Canonical is correct and hreflang is well-formed
question: Does each product page name itself as the URL to index, so the index holds the page the agent was sent to?
method: Read rel=canonical from the HTML and from the Link response header of each sampled product page that answered. Problems are checked in this order, and the first one found sets the verdict. Fail when a page carries no canonical. Warn when a page carries several or conflicting canonicals, a relative canonical, a canonical on another host, a canonical on http while the page is https, or a canonical naming a different URL than the one that answered (the sampled page is then a duplicate and the other URL is what gets indexed, so sitemaps should list that one). For hreflang alternates, warn when they appear on some sampled pages only, when an alternate URL is relative, or when a page names fewer than two languages and no x-default. The alternate pages are not fetched, so reciprocity is not judged. Pass when every sampled page's canonical is absolute and resolves to the page itself. Skipped when no product page was sampled or none could be fetched.

title: Accessible main content
question: Is the product content inside a main landmark, with no cookie or consent banner before it in the HTML?
method: Informational. Read each sampled product page that answered (the home page when none were sampled). Pass when every page has a main landmark (a main element or an element with role=main) and no cookie or consent banner comes before it in document order. Warn when a page has no main landmark, or when a banner precedes it, naming the element. A banner is an element whose class or id contains cookie, consent, gdpr, privacy-banner or the token cmp. Elements that render nothing (script, style, template and similar) and generic names such as modal, overlay or drawer do not count, so a cart drawer or a closed modal is not reported. No answer engine documents depending on landmarks, so this is reported and never scored.

spec.title: WAI-ARIA 1.2: landmark roles

title: Unknown URLs answer 404
question: Does the site tell an agent honestly when a page does not exist?
method: GET a fixed path under the origin that cannot exist (/agentic-readiness-probe- plus a code derived from the host name). Pass on 404 or 410, whatever the body. Fail when the server answers 200 with an HTML page (a soft 404): an agent then reads a page that does not exist as if it did, and every stale link it follows looks like content. Warn on a redirect to the home page, on any other redirect, and on any other status (such as 403, 500 or a 200 that is not HTML). Skipped when the probe is rate limited (429), meets a gateway error (502, 503, 504) or gets no response: such an answer says nothing about 404 handling, and a 429 is not a soft 404.

spec.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors (soft 404)
RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics

title: Product URLs answer directly over HTTPS
question: Do the URLs the site publishes answer 200 at that address, and does every variant of the host lead to it?
method: Fetch each sampled product URL (taken from the sitemap or the home page, the home page itself when none was found) and record the redirect hops to the final answer. Then GET the http:// form of the origin and the other host variant (www or apex), which should each redirect to the canonical origin. Fail when a redirect leaves HTTPS for HTTP, when a chain exceeds the five hops the scanner follows (Google stops at ten), or when a URL taken from the sitemap answers 404 or 410: Google asks that sitemaps list only live, canonical URLs, and Bing asks publishers to remove deleted or redirected URLs promptly. Warn when a published URL redirects before it answers, even by one hop (the sitemap or link should name the final URL, since Google indexes the redirect target and Bing asks for canonical URLs in sitemaps). Warn when a URL answers a status other than 200 without redirecting. Warn when a host variant serves its own content with 200, answers another status, or redirects to a host other than the canonical origin (a host of the same registrable domain is reported as consolidation elsewhere). Pass when every URL answers 200 at its own address and neither variant contradicts it. When the home page stands in for product URLs, a hop that changes the host plus one redirect from / to a locale or landing path is not a finding. A host variant that answers 429, a gateway error or nothing is inconclusive and not held against the store. Skipped when none of the sampled URLs could be fetched. Every redirect reported names the URL it left and the one it reached.

spec.title: Google: how to specify a canonical (HTTPS preference, redirects)

title: Title and description on every page
question: Does every page name itself, so a citation has a title and the index has a description?
method: Read the <title> element and the meta description of the home page, the sampled listing page and each sampled product page that answered. Pages that did not answer are recorded, not judged. Fail when any page has no title or an empty one: the title is the one field every answer engine returns with a citation, and Bing ties missing titles to grounding eligibility. Warn, in this order, when two pages share a title (ignoring case and spacing), when a title is shorter than ten characters, or when a page has no meta description or an empty one. Bing names short or missing descriptions as reducing eligibility, and Google uses the description for some snippets. Length maxima are not judged: no engine documents one.

spec.title: Bing Webmaster Guidelines (search, Copilot and grounding)

title: Conditional requests supported
question: Can a crawler ask whether a product page changed instead of downloading it again?
method: Read the ETag and Last-Modified headers of the HTML response of the first sampled product page that answered (the home page when none were sampled). A Markdown copy negotiated with Accept: text/markdown is never judged, because converters serve it without validators. When a validator is present, GET the page again with If-None-Match (for an ETag) or If-Modified-Since (for a date) and expect 304. Pass on 304. Warn when the server answers 200 to the conditional request (the validator is decorative), when it answers another status, or when it sends no validator at all. Google's crawlers and Bing both name ETags as the way they detect unchanged pages. Skipped when the page or the conditional request could not be fetched.

title: Mobile viewport declared
question: Does the page declare itself usable on a phone, which is the device Google indexes with?
method: Read the meta viewport of each sampled product page that answered (the home page when none were sampled). Google crawls and indexes with the smartphone crawler only and documents the viewport tag as the signal that a page is mobile friendly. A site not accessible on a mobile device is no longer indexable. Pass when every page declares width=device-width and allows zooming. Warn when a page has no viewport tag, a tag without width=device-width (such as a fixed pixel width), or a tag that forbids zooming (user-scalable=no or 0, or maximum-scale below 1). The scanner does not render pages, so content parity between desktop and mobile is not judged.

spec.title: Google Search Central blog: mobile-first indexing, the last step (2024)
Google: meta tags and attributes that Google supports (viewport)

title: Document head is well-formed
question: Will a crawler see the title, canonical and directives where the page put them?
method: Scan the raw HTML of each sampled product page that answered with a body (the home page when none were sampled) in document order. Google reads the head only up to the first element that does not belong there (anything but title, meta, link, script, style, base, noscript and template) and ignores metadata after it. Browsers do the same when they close the head early. Fail when a meta refresh that names a URL has a delay of five seconds or less, which turns the page into a redirect. Fail when a <title>, rel=canonical, robots or description meta, or hreflang alternate appears after such an element or inside the body. Warn when the page is not served as text/html (or application/xhtml+xml), when the document lacks the HTML doctype (<!doctype html>), or when no character encoding is declared in the Content-Type header or within the first 1024 bytes. The rules run in that order. Pass otherwise. Titles and metadata inside inline SVG or MathML are an icon's accessible name, not document metadata, and are ignored. Skipped when no page answered with a body.

spec.title: Google: valid page metadata (what Google reads in the head)

title: PrestaShop friendly URLs
question: Do PrestaShop product URLs carry readable paths instead of query strings?
method: Runs only on PrestaShop stores. Look at the sampled product URLs. Pass when every one is a readable path. Warn when any is a query-string URL (one with an id_product or controller parameter, or an index.php path), which PrestaShop builds when Friendly URL is off under Shop Parameters > Traffic & SEO. Readable URLs tell an agent what the page is before it fetches it and stay stable across parameters. Skipped when no product page was sampled. No extra request.

spec.title: PrestaShop 9 user guide: SEO and URLs
Google Search Central: URL structure best practices

title: Ecwid store pages have their own URLs
question: Do the Ecwid store's product pages have URLs a crawler can fetch?
method: Runs only on sites with an Ecwid store. Read the home page. Warn when any store link uses a hashbang URL (/store/#!/product-name/p/123456), because the part after #! never reaches the server. Otherwise pass on Instant Site and on WordPress and Wix sites, where Ecwid documents clean URLs and static copies of product pages as automatic, or when the integration code switches clean URLs on (window.ec.config.storefrontUrls.cleanUrls = true). Warn when the store is embedded in a custom site whose integration code does not switch clean URLs on. No extra request.

spec.title: Ecwid Help Center: What Ecwid does for SEO
